newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss giant Novartis sees strong '97 profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Swiss giant Novartis sees strong '97 profit growth.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals and chemicals giant Novartis AG said Tuesday its 1996 operating income edged higher, forecast strong 1997 profit growth and reassured investors that its merger was proceeding smoothly.

Novartis, the world's second-biggest pharmaceutical company, was formed by the merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG last year. It had forecast 1996 earnings, excluding one-time merger-related expenses, would be about the same as in 1995.

Novartis reported a 1996 group net profit of 2.304 billion Swiss francs ($1.6 billion) vs. 4.216 billion ($2.9 billion) in 1995. Net profit before one-time items edged up to 4.175 billion ($2.9 billion) from 4.096 billion ($2.8 billion).
Total sales, including divested operations, rose to 36.23 billion francs ($24.9 billion) from 35.94 billion ($24.6 billion). Operating income rose 4 percent.

"In 1997, we should ... experience a strong positive currency effect. Together with the realisation of the merger synthesis, this should lead, barring any unforeseen events, to a marked improvement of operating and net income," it said in a statement.

Analysts had already discounted the results and were more eager for news on progress in integrating the two companies, whose combination created the world's biggest pharmaceutical company after Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
Novartis said it had achieved all the goals it set for 1996 and had also seen dynamic growth in all divisions during the first two months of this year.
After divestitures, net merger-related charges were 1.9 billion francs ($1.3 billion) after taxes, also in line with forecasts.
Novartis, which proposed a dividend increase to 20 Swiss francs (13.7 cents) per share from 16.80 (11.5 cents), said it expected to finish most of its integration projects this year.
Novartis said growth of its established key products continued to be strong and new products were becoming more important, thanks to an aggressive programme of product launches.
It boosted marketing spending 7 percent last year to support product launches and expanded its sales force.
Executives told a news conference in London that Novartis has 85 pharmaceutical projects in clinical development and plans to launch 29 new products in the next three years.
By comparison, Glaxo-Wellcome plans to launch some 20 new products within the next four years.
Novartis said last year's sales in the core "life sciences" business -- pharmaceuticals, agribusiness and nutrition -- rose 8 percent to 27.60 billion francs ($18.9 billion).
Group research and development spending rose by 4 percent.
